chapter_name: Chapter 20: Long Composition: Letters, Paragraphs, and Emails
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn to structure long-form writing, differentiating between formal and informal letters, structuring cohesive paragraphs, and drafting professional digital emails.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Sometimes a few words just aren't enough! Whether you are writing a heartfelt letter to a friend, a formal application to the principal, or a modern digital email, you need a strong structure to keep the reader engaged. Let's master the art of long-form writing!

lesson_modules.module_title: ✉️ Formal vs. Informal Letters (औपचारिक और अनौपचारिक पत्र)
lesson_modules.teaching_content: Informal letters are to friends/family (casual tone, only sender's address needed). Formal letters are to officials or businesses (respectful tone, strictly formatted). A Formal Letter requires: Sender's Address -> Date -> Receiver's Address -> Subject -> Salutation -> Body -> Subscription (Yours faithfully).
examples_or_templates:
Formal: Yours faithfully/sincerely, [Full Name] 
(Don't forget the 'Subject' line in a formal letter!)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A good paragraph is like a perfectly stacked burger. The top bun is the 'Topic Sentence' (introduces the main idea). The meat is the 'Supporting Sentences' (gives examples, facts, or reasons). The bottom bun is the 'Concluding Sentence' (wraps up the idea).
examples_or_templates: Topic Sentence: 'Trees are our best friends.'
Supporting Details: 'They give us oxygen, provide shade, and bear fruits.'
Concluding Sentence: 'Therefore, we must protect trees at all costs.'

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Emails are the digital version of letters. They are fast and concise. The format includes: 'To:' (Receiver's email address), 'Subject:' (A very short summary of the email), Salutation, Body, and Sign-off. The subject line is the most important part—it decides if the person will open the email!
examples_or_templates: Subject: Request for 2 days of sick leave.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ In a Formal Letter, where is the Receiver's Address placed?
options: Inside the body of the letter

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ What is the most critical part of the Email header that tells the reader what the email is about?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a clear and concise 'Subject' line for a formal letter complaining about frequent power cuts in your area.
✍️ Write a 'Topic Sentence' for a paragraph about the importance of reading books.
subjective_practice.hint: Make a strong statement that introduces the magic of reading.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ What is the correct 'Subscription' (sign-off) for a formal letter to your school Principal?
subjective_practice.hint: You shouldn't use 'Yours lovingly'. Use something respectful.

activity_or_assignment.title: 💻 The Digital Pen Pal
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Draft a proper Email on a piece of paper (or type it out if you have access to a computer) to your English teacher. In the Subject line, write 'Thank you for a great class!'. Write 3 sentences in the body telling them what your favorite grammar topic was this year, and sign off with 'Regards, [Your Name]'.

chapter_summary: ⭐ Formal letters require both sender and receiver addresses, a subject line, and a respectful tone.
⭐ A well-structured paragraph always has a Topic Sentence, Supporting Sentences, and a Concluding Sentence.
⭐ Emails are digital letters that rely on a strong, clear 'Subject' line to inform the reader of the content.
